fieldValues.title: An ext:*-titled subsection can be the ONLY resolver for its RFC-integration ext: token, with no dedicated extension shadow record backing it up
fieldValues.summary: check-rfc-integration.mjs resolves an `ext:<name>` manifest token against either a `com.semanticops.spec/extension` record's extension_id field, OR, as a fallback, any subsection record whose title starts with `ext:` (the 'retired extension shadow's subsection twin' rule). Ten of the current ext:* subsections already have a dedicated extension shadow record as a safety net; ext:type-inheritance did not. Deleting it under srs#710 broke RFC-020 and RFC-040's ext:type-inheritance token with no warning until validate-all was actually run.
evidence: srs/records/extensions/ contains exactly 10 com.semanticops.spec/extension shadow records (ext:slices, ext:import-tracking, ext:changelog, ext:views-l2, ext:discovery, ext:themes-l1, ext:cross-field-validation, ext:views-l1, ext:recommended-relations, ext:lifecycle) as of this unit's start.

The 50 subsection records remaining at this unit's start included 4 pure ext:*-titled ones with no matching extension shadow record: ext:type-inheritance, ext:protocol, ext:repository, ext:federation.

Deleting subsection 37e2f653 (ext:type-inheritance) via record delete --cascade, then running node scripts/validate-all.mjs with its real exit code captured (not piped through tail), produced: 'RFC-020: manifest token "ext:type-inheritance" does not resolve to any canonical record/schema' and the same for RFC-040 -- both cite ext:type-inheritance inside an actual <!-- srs-integration:v1 --> block.

Creating srs/records/extensions/extension-58707681.json (extension_id: ext:type-inheritance, retirement-stub content pointing at the Type specialisation concept) and excluding it in scripts/publication-reachability-exclusions.json made validate-all pass again.

Grepped srs/records/tier-2/rfc-*.json for a real srs-integration manifest citation of ext:protocol, ext:repository, or ext:federation: zero hits inside an actual manifest block (only unrelated decision-record prose mentions ext:protocol). So those three are a latent version of the same gap, not an active break, as of this unit.
fieldValues.body:
The asymmetry: when batches #561-564 originally split a subsection's prose into mechanism/example leaves, an extension shadow record was created separately and independently for MOST ext:* extensions (by earlier work resolving srs#285/#407/#411), as a deliberate safety net so check-rfc-integration.mjs's ext: token resolution would survive the eventual subsection deletion. ext:type-inheritance never got that treatment -- nothing in the corpus or its own migration batch created a shadow for it, so its token resolution silently depended on the subsection record surviving, which srs#710 explicitly plans to delete.

This is invisible until the subsection is actually deleted and validate-all is run for real: repo validate stays green (extension_id resolution isn't a repo-validate concern), and nothing else signals the gap in advance. The only reliable detection is exactly what this unit did after the fact -- delete, then run the real gate, read the failure, fix, re-verify -- or, better, checking in advance: before deleting any ext:*-titled subsection, confirm a matching com.semanticops.spec/extension shadow record already exists (grep records/extensions/ for the extension_id), and if not, check whether any RFC's srs-integration manifest actually cites that ext:<name> token before assuming it's safe to skip creating one.

Related but distinct from carried-context-87e8e448/c4e43a58 (orphaned example leaves, stale section:/subsection: RFC tokens): this is specifically about the ext: token kind's OWN resolution path having a hidden, per-extension single point of failure.
